prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that at the Petersons' potluck, you presented a store-bought dish in your own cookware. Respond to the committee.
response:
MR. CHAIRMAN, DISTINGUISHED MEMBERS OF THE COMMITTEE—

I come before you today as a patriot and a lifelong participant in the American potluck tradition. And I say to you, without hesitation: I have never been, nor am I now, a member of the Tupperware Deception Conspiracy.

*[adjusts microphone]*

Now, let me address the so-called "Peterson Potluck Incident" directly. Yes, I attended. Yes, I brought a seven-layer dip. And yes—I will not deny it—that dip arrived in my own ceramic dish, the one with the little painted lemons on it.

But I must ask this committee: since WHEN is owning attractive cookware a CRIME in this country?

*[leans forward]*

The prosecution would have you believe that the mere PRESENCE of an attractive dish implies GUILT. That a woman cannot possess a nice serving vessel without intent to deceive. I reject this premise. I reject it wholesale.

**Point of order:** I request that the record reflect the plastic container was found in my recycling bin, NOT hidden. Not buried. Not incinerated in some frantic midnight cover-up. If I were guilty, Mr. Chairman, would I have LEFT THE EVIDENCE for the raccoons?

*[dramatic pause]*

I invoke my rights. I decline to name the other attendees who "bought and told." I will NOT participate in a witch hunt against the Hendersons, whose "homemade" coleslaw came from a bag, and everyone at this table knows it.

I stand by my dip. I stand by my dish.

And I stand by the Fifth Amendment, should we get to the part about the "homemade" pie crust.

I yield the remainder of my time.
